ppi_focus: Rear subframe mounts and trunk-floor spot welds (especially left), diff ears: look for cracks or tearing.
Rust survey of the rockers, jack pads, floor pans, subframe mounts and hatch seams (Northeast car).
Cooling system: pressure test; check the radiator end tanks, expansion tank, water pump play and thermostat housing for weeps.
Oil filter housing gasket, valve cover gasket and oil pan for leaks; check the DISA valve for rattle.
VANOS: listen at cold idle for rattle and scan for VANOS/cam fault codes.
Clutch engagement point, slip test, and shifter bushing play.
Rear trailing-arm bushings and front control-arm bushings.
Tire date codes and even wear (alignment).
Hatch seal and hatch struts; check for water in the spare-wheel well and cargo floor.
Match the VIN to the title and door jamb; read the emissions label for CA compliance; check the odometer against records.
what_would_change_verdict: Up: clean title, VIN history consistent with 86k miles, and dated cooling-system invoices.
Up: photos or a specialist PPI showing an intact trunk floor, rear subframe and rust-free underside.
Down: cracked trunk-floor welds, subframe rust or significant rocker or floor rust.
Down: branded title, unreported accident evidence, refusal of VIN or PPI, or a 49-state-only emissions label blocking CA registration.
Down: tires older than six years, active leaks or VANOS faults found at PPI, which would add known work.
evidence.mission_note: A manual M54 Z3 coupe squarely fits the enthusiast-bridge brief, with strong resale in 6-24 months, at a price inside the ceiling but above the ideal band. In accelerated_bridge mode the RX covers daily needs, so there is time to insist on the VIN, structure photos and a PPI before committing.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a 2001 Z3 3.0i coupe, manual, silver over red, with 86,000 claimed miles, asking $21,500 after a $5,000 cut. The photos support the body style, manual gearbox, stock appearance, clean wheels and tidy engine bay. They also show visible leather creasing on both seats, which softens the 'excellent interior' claim. Nothing verifiable beyond the photos is provided: no VIN, title, accident or owner information, and no service records. Both model-critical items are missing: no rear-structure or trunk-floor evidence on a Massachusetts car, and no cooling-system history at an age and mileage where it is due. Against the $24,165-$25,834 fair-value band and coupe sales of $26,000 at 84k miles and $18,000 at 99k miles, the asking price sits below the market midpoint. That is only meaningful if the structure, rust and title check out. The reason for the removal and relist is unknown.
evidence.next_action: Message the seller for the VIN, a title photo, trunk-floor and underside photos, tire date codes and any cooling-system invoices, and confirm he will allow a BMW-specialist PPI near Deerfield before any deposit.
